## 1. Build explain a change in library visits

Week 1 visits Monday to Friday are 10, 20, 15, 25, 30; week 2 values are 12, 18, missing, 30, 40. A new display opened in week 2. Preserve missingness, compare the four matched days, and also report incomplete raw weekly totals. Create a day-by-day plot and a report for a volunteer.

Predict an ordinary result before coding. Start with the smallest part you can
run and inspect. Use Colab for notebooks and the local workspace introduced in
the units for packaging or command-line tasks.

## 2. Set up the experiment

```python
import pandas as pd

visits = pd.DataFrame({
    "day": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri"],
    "week_1": [10, 20, 15, 25, 30],
    "week_2": [12, 18, None, 30, 40],
})
# Compare raw totals and matched days explicitly.
```

The starter is deliberately incomplete. Implement the contract; do not change
the expected results to match an incorrect implementation.

## 3. Check the observable results

1. Week 1 has five observations totaling 100; week 2 has four observed values totaling 100.
2. Matched-day totals are 85 and 100: an increase of 15, approximately 17.65%.
3. Wednesday remains missing in the source and plot, not zero.
4. Report counts with totals and explain why raw totals are not a like-for-like comparison.

Record actual outputs beside predictions. Reduce a failure to a small example,
change one cause at a time, and repeat the failed check after repairing it.

## 4. Change one condition

Recover Wednesday as 5 in one scenario and 35 in another. Recompute complete weekly comparisons. Explain how a conclusion based only on the original totals could mislead.

## 5. Review a hint after attempting the task

<details>
<summary>Hint: connect the relevant tools</summary>

Apply a matched-day mask before comparable aggregation. Keep recovered-value scenarios separate from observed data and annotate missingness.

</details>

## 6. Explain and self-review

Deliver the notebook, missingness audit, comparison table, plot, and a 150-word report. Mention weather, events, and recording differences as reasons the observation alone cannot establish the display caused the change.

<details>
<summary>Review path: compare your result with the contract</summary>

Check the ordinary result first, then the boundary cases and changed condition.
Explain which rule justifies each result. An implementation that differs from
the hint can still satisfy the contract; explain why yours does.

</details>
